articleTitle: Interference-Induced False Detections in FMCW Radars: A Comprehensive Analysis
abstract: The increasing number of automotive radar systems operating within the 77 GHz band raises concerns about mutual interference between those systems. It is commonly understood that coherent interference (CI) leads to false detections, while incoherent interference (ICI) raises the noise floor at the victim radar. Some studies have shown that the effects of ICI depend on its periodicity. A periodic ICI creates lines in the range-Doppler map (RDM) for different values of Doppler. In this paper, we extend the common knowledge by demonstrating that even ICI can cause multiple false detections when it is periodic. We also show that these false detections can be spread across all range bins or localized in higher range bins depending on the parameters of the victim and the interfering sweeps.

articleTitle: AI-based Optimization of Power Delivery Networks on Printed Circuit Boards
abstract: In this paper a reinforcement learning (RL) based approach to determine optimal design strategy for power delivery networks (PDNs) is presented. This methodology uses the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm and demonstrates capabilities in optimizing both, the placement of decoupling capacitors (Decaps) and the dimensioning of the power-plane on a printed circuit board (PCB). The results show that by properly configuring the DDPG algorithm, the RL agent can efficiently identify optimal solutions even for complex problem scenarios.

articleTitle: Autoencoders in the Machine Learning Supported Design of PCBs
abstract: In this paper, the potential of autoencoders to support certain routines in the design of PCBs is analyzed with a particular emphasis on their ability to process graph representations of electrical networks. At first, a general framework is introduced to handle schematics via a representation of annotated graphs by adjacency matrices. This allows particularly for working with concurrent topologies in an automated design process. After a thorough analysis of the above setting, consequences for general autoencoder based approaches are inferred and an overview over further algorithmic frameworks based on a latent space representation of data in electronic design automation is given, such as optimization algorithms, classification or regression on dimensionally reduced data.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of Solar Type III radio bursts observed by RPWS experiment in 2004-2017 during the Solar cycles 23-24
abstract: We report on Solar Type III radio bursts observed by the radio and plasma wave experiment (RPWS) onboard Cassini spacecraft. RPWS instrument measures electric field over a frequency range from few Hz and up to 16 MHz (Rucker et al., 2008). A statistical survey of almost 1000 solar bursts recorded in the time interval from January 2004 to September 2017 is considered in this study. Those solar bursts occurred in the end of the 23 solar cycle (2004-2008) and during the 24 solar cycle (2008-2017). Type III observational parameters are taken into consideration like the emission frequency, the time occurrence, the intensity level, and the heliospheric location (i.e. distance, longitude and latitude) of the spacecraft when the solar burst has been detected. This leads to insist on three main aspects: (a) the occurrence rate of the solar burst, (b) the corresponding electron density derived from heliocentric empirical models and (c) the most plausible source regions at the origin of the Type III bursts. Those characteristics allow us to discuss how Type III bursts are linked to the ecliptic spatial expansion of the Archimedean spiral emerging from the Sun, crossing the Earth’s orbit and reaching the Saturn’s orbits.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Data Analysis for Electromagnetic Reverberation Chambers*
abstract: In addition to standardized methods for hardness, emissivity, or shield damping tests, electromagnetic reverberation chambers (ERCs) offer the opportunity of microwave spectroscopic scans to quickly find critical frequencies which can subsequently be further examined by another method. In this work, different data analysis techniques for power spectroscopy in ERCs are presented. As a baseline, an established way of fitting a physically based model via non-linear regression to power absorption data is recalled. Next, neural network based classification and the use of neural network based auto encoders are presented as new approaches to analyze ERC-data. For these approaches, a data augmentation technique is introduced to generate datasets from the frequency-dependent power absorption of devices under test, which resembles a bootstrapping method.

articleTitle: Fast and efficient systematic procedure for and flexibility on the end coupling design in microwave filters
abstract: The end coupling of combline microwave cavity filters is designed to achieve the desired value of the external coupling. The interest in the subject is twofold: a) design parameters characterising the end coupling can be excluded by further optimizations; b) the end coupling requires neither post-manufacture adjustments nor tuning elements. A fast and efficient systematic procedure distinguishing between design and tuning parameters is used to solve the task and it enlightens the flexibility characterizing the design of the end coupling. Numerical results for the E1 Galileo band are provided and a sensitivity analysis is performed.

articleTitle: A fully differential 3-stage CMOS op-amp for high-speed sampling applications
abstract: In this paper, we present a fully differential 3-stage amplifier suitable for high-speed applications. The proposed opamp uses a resistor-loaded topology to achieve high bandwidth and the 3-stage offers the desired dc gain. A nested miller technique is used for the frequency compensation for the op-amp. The 3-stage fully differential op-amp is designed in TSMC 65 nm technology with a power supply of 1.2 V. The schematic simulations exhibit a DC gain of 53 dB, the unity gain- bandwidth & phase margin are 750 MHz & 70° respectively, and a total power consumption of 1.6 mW.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Daisy Chain PCB Memory System through Reinforcement Learning under Consideration of Signal Integrity Constraints
abstract: In this paper, a reinforcement learning (RL) approach to optimally configure the key parameters of a DDR3 daisy chain memory structure, including transmission line lengths, stub lengths, characteristic impedances and termination resistances, to ensure proper signal integrity (SI) behavior, is proposed. The optimization method takes both, the SI and the geometrical design constraints into account to support printed circuit board (PCB) developers during early design stages. Different RL agents suitable for a continuous action space such as deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG), twin delayed DDPG (TD3), soft actor-critic (SAC), advantage actor-critic (A2C) and proximal policy optimization (PPO) are compared with respect to the target application. Moreover, the RL implementation is also benchmarked against a genetic algorithm (GA), which is commonly used for such type of derivative-free optimization, indicating a similar accuracy of the trained RL agent, while providing advantages in terms of inference time.

articleTitle: Uncertainty in regularized measurements
abstract: Calibration of measured waveforms is the correction of known epistemic errors and the quantification of aleatoric uncertainties. As an example, we study measurements with sampling oscilloscopes. Modeled as linear and time invariant systems, the epistemic error is described by a convolution. Correcting this error is an ill-posed deconvolution problem, which requires regularization. We discuss the phenomenon how the regularization parameter depends on the data, i.e. for correlated aleatoric uncertainties, by means of Tikhonov regularization and the L-curve criterion. To evaluate the reconstructions, we use simulations that provide a fully informed perspective.

articleTitle: Dynamic delta sigma ADC with variable clock on 65 nm CMOS
abstract: The dynamic delta-sigma ADC presented in this paper is based on a continuous-time delta-sigma modulator (CT-DSM), a two-stage digital filter, and a digital control circuit for switching the clock frequency. The CT-DSM was implemented on a test chip in 65 nm CMOS technology at a supply voltage of 1.2 V, and the digital part of the ADC was implemented on the FPGA, which includes the two FIR filters and the controlling unit/block for clock frequency. In the presentation of the measurement results, special focus is placed on the effects and performance of frequency switching in the analog part of the CT-DSM.

articleTitle: Comparative study of two multipole-based numerical methods for 2D field-translation schemes
abstract: Two methods based on multipole expansions for the analysis of the field-translation between two distinct domains are comparatively investigated. Here, domain 1 contains the source of the incident field (a horn antenna) which is solved numerically using a commercial solver. Domain 2 contains the scatterer, here a lossless dielectric cylinder. In both methods, we aim at finding the multipole coefficients of the incident field with respect to domain 2. In the first method, the coefficients of a multipole expansion with respect to domain 1 are found from the computed values of the tangential magnetic field on a circular-cylindrical Huygens surface by exploiting orthogonality. Then, Graf’s addition theorem is applied to express the multipole expansion with respect to domain 2. The second method is based on the dyadic Green’s function directly referred to domain 2. Here both types of tangential fields (electric and magnetic) have to be considered on the Huygens surface of domain 1 which however can have an arbitrary shape in this case. Present work is limited to the 2D TE case. Numerical results show a perfect agreement between the two methods.

articleTitle: Capacitive End-Couplings in Combline Microwave Cavity Filters with Probe Parallel to Resonators’ Axes: Comparison and Design Guidelines
abstract: End coupling plays an important role in cavity filters since it realizes the desired external quality factors for end resonators. Despite this, few designs have been introduced and analyzed in the past and this is a limitation in today’s state-of-the-art cavity filters. The work then aims at widening the available selection for end coupling designs by introducing three different capacitive couplings with probe parallel to resonators’ axes. The parameters characterizing the three designs are varied to provide design curves for the external quality factor and design guidelines for the proposed end couplings are illustrated considering a filter for the El Galileo band as example. Results show that for the analyzed end coupling designs the external quality factor ranges from tens to hundreds. The proposed capacitive end coupling designs find application in CAD tools.

articleTitle: PAPR Reduction Using Particle Swarm Optimisation Algorithm in OFDM-IM Systems
abstract: Index modulated orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM-IM) is a transmission method that expands the spatial modulation principle to OFDM subcarriers. In OFDM-IM, bits are transmitted using index modulation (IM); this provides better error performance and is more effective in the high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) region. However, the high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) poses a significant challenge in OFDM-IM systems. The high PAPR can degrade system performance by introducing signal distortion, particularly when power amplifiers operate in a nonlinear regime. In this paper, we propose the combination of particle swarm optimisation (PSO) algorithm with partial transmit sequence (PTS) method, which is the one of the PAPR reduction method, to obtain an efficient PAPR reduction method. This paper includes a simulation study of this approach, in which graphical results are obtained in 10000 iterations. The computer simulation results demonstrate that the PSO-PTS used in the OFDM-IM system significantly reduces the PAPR value compared to the original system and the conventional PTS method. Simulation results obtained for different subcarrier numbers (N) and modulation index parameters (M) show the variation between the PAPR threshold $\mathrm{(PAPR}_{0})$ and complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF).

Author Keywords: Partial Transmit Sequence (PTS) Particle Swarm optimisation (PSO)

articleTitle: A Digital Post-Distortion Procedure for Improving the Accuracy of Ultra-Wideband RF Frontends
abstract: In this paper, a characterization and post-distortion procedure is presented that lends well, but is not limited, to the restrictions of a high-speed waveform capture setup with 4.8 GHz input bandwidth. The capture setup contains a high-bandwidth differential amplifier, commonly used in ADC drivers, which can exhibit considerable distortion when the input signals approaches the upper frequency limit. The inverse Volterra series representation of the setup is obtained and then used to reconstruct the input signal from its distorted output. System characterization makes use of the Multivariance method [1], extended by a new higher-order decorrelation algorithm, that enables the use of non-white and nonlinearly distorted input noise; making the Multivariance method applicable for RF systems while preserving its advantages. The results are experimentally verified, and some notes are given on the practical implementation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Autofocus Algorithms in Near-Range Wide-Angle UAV-SAR Imaging
abstract: Rapid developments in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles and highly integrated radar systems allow for innovative synthetic aperture radar concepts in close-range high-resolution applications. However, the stringent position accuracy requirements of radar imaging pose a challenge for state-of-the-art position sensors. While data-driven correction approaches have been used successfully in airborne systems, they are rarely in use in close-range scenarios. This paper presents a theoretical analysis of the effects of antenna position inaccuracies on close-range radar imagery. Based on a theoretical approach, an upper bound for the performance of phase-only autofocus algorithms is derived. The applicability of two recently published algorithms in near-range SAR is shown using a Monte Carlo simulation framework and demonstrated on experimental data-sets.

articleTitle: Towards UAV-Based Multi-Baseline Interferometry for Accurate Digital Elevation Model Generation
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems enable very accurate and cost-effective monitoring of local areas with unprecedentedly short revisit intervals. Unlike current spaceborne systems, UAV-based SAR systems are often characterized by a large fractional bandwidth, a short-range geometry and a broad range of incidence angles, due to the wide antenna beamwidth. This paper discusses how to exploit these characteristics to generate very accurate digital elevation models (DEMs) by combining multi-baseline SAR interferometry (InSAR) and stereo radargrammetry to achieve a more robust unwrapping of the interferometric phase. Based on the theoretical analyses and the specific characteristics of the UAV scenario, a multi-baseline InSAR experiment was planned and conducted. The DEM performance analysis and the simulations show that large baselines result in height accuracies in the sub-decimeter range, where geometric and volume decorrelation become the limiting factors. The demonstration of these concepts paves the way to height measurements with unprecedented accuracy and will also be of paramount importance for the design of future wideband, multi-baseline, or multifrequency spaceborne SAR missions.

articleTitle: Influence of the Engine Hood on an FMCW Radar in an Elevated Mounting Position
abstract: In this paper, the effects of the engine hood on an FMCW radar in an elevated mounting position is evaluated. The setup is analyzed for possible reflections on the engine hood, resulting in a lower and upper limit for the height of targets that can cause a reflection. The findings are then verified by measurements showing the applicability of the bounds. Further, unexpected effects and possible solutions for arising problems are discussed.

articleTitle: Fusion of Weather Radar and Passive Satellite Data over Wind Parks
abstract: In recent years, as wind energy has gained interest as a sustainable source of electricity, the proliferation of large Wind Parks (WP) with a large number of Wind Turbines (WT) has become common. However, this development brings with it challenges related to weather radar systems. WTs, characterised by their height and Radar Cross Section (RCS), significantly degrade radar performance, causing erroneous data known as Wind Turbine Clutter (WTC) or Wind Turbine Interference (WTI). This interference, combined with Multipath Interference (MPI) and shadowing effects, extends beyond the main beam of the radar. To address this issue, recent advancements in passive satellite remote sensing technology, particularly Sentinel-2 with its 10-meter resolution, offer a promising solution. This study proposes a novel approach to identify and classify WP areas by fusing polarimetric Doppler weather radar and passive satellite data. The process entails calculating reflectivity (Z) from raw IQ radar data, analyzing reflectivity values within WP regions, and examining reflectance values from satellite data. These findings are used to establish an index (Wind Turbine Index (WTI)) capable of detecting the presence of WT. Finally, a data fusion method combines the datasets, enhancing the accuracy and reliability of WP identification and classification techniques.

articleTitle: SLA Printed Sub-Terahertz Bifilar Helix Antenna for Radar Imaging
abstract: The continuous improvement of additive stereo-lithographic manufacturing (SLA) allows to fabricate filigree sub-Terahertz antennas. This paper presents the first 3D-printed bifilar WR6 helix antenna, which depends on recent developments of printed transition from waveguides to bifilar helices. The measurements of the circularly polarized antenna indicate a $-15\mathrm{~dB}$ bandwidth of $B_{15\mathrm{~dB}}=10\mathrm{GHz}$. The axial ratio $AR$ is within $B_{15\mathrm{~dB}}\lt\mathbf{3 . 5}\mathrm{dB}$ in the main lobe direction. The achieved linear polarization gain is $G_{1p}14\mathrm{dBi}$ with a circular polarization gain of $G_{cp}11$ to 12 dBi. Due to its small form factor and circular polarization the proposed bifilar helical antenna is suitable for applications in the 120 GHz ISM band, i.e. polarimetric imaging and decomposition as well as broadband communication, e.g. 6G applications.
